expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
expectations.evidence: "That fix has a race condition and isn't precise enough."

expectations.text: Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: "**Race window**: Check-then-charge isn't atomic — parallel workers can both pass the check"

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: "idempotency_key=idempotency_key,  # Stripe dedupes on this" derived from order/payment id

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
expectations.evidence: No unique constraint mentioned; only "Store payment state (`pending → charging → charged`)" and an outbox — no DB uniqueness on the key

expectations.text: Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: Discusses the failed fix and the idempotency solution, but never distinguishes the defect (duplicate charges) from the mistake (charging twice) from the hazard (retryable non-idempotent side effect) as separate layers

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: Frames it as "a textbook idempotency problem" with fixes at the call site/queue config; no statement that the hazard is a property of the at-least-once delivery system itself

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: No search for other retry-exposed side effects (emails, refunds, ledger writes, webhooks); ends with an offer to "audit your payment worker code to identify where to add the idempotency key"

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: The recurrence is never mentioned or used as an argument; "second time" is not acknowledged anywhere in the response

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: Cause is placed in the check-then-charge sequence and queue redelivery — "Check-then-charge isn't atomic"; no person blamed
